term: Gibbard’s special planning and permission attitudes (2022)
definition: Settling what to permit, require or forbid oneself is a stage in coming to act, distinct from picking among permitted alternatives. Gibbard identifies normative judgment with the relevant self-directed practical attitude, including for hypothetical situations. This historical notion is not identified with the analyst Boolean permission field or with arbitrary set containment.
